input_sources.text: Gateway GW-19 uses a Raspberry Pi 5 with its fan-control defaults unchanged. During warm-up from a cold start, the reported temperature rose from 35 to 45 degrees Celsius; the fan remained off. No repair or parts use was recorded.

Raspberry Pi 5 defaults keep the fan off below 50 degrees Celsius during warming. Speeds at 50, 60, 67.5, and 75 degrees Celsius are respectively 30%, 50%, 70%, and 100%. Configuration can change these defaults.
input_sources.attribution: Raspberry Pi Ltd; passages summarized by the project assistant.

input_sources.text: As Raspberry Pi 5 cools, fan-speed reductions occur 5 degrees Celsius below the warming thresholds. This hysteresis and the speed thresholds are configurable.
input_sources.attribution: Raspberry Pi Ltd; passages summarized by the project assistant.

original_sources.text: Gateway GW-19 uses a Raspberry Pi 5 with its fan-control defaults unchanged. During warm-up from a cold start, the reported temperature rose from 35 to 45 degrees Celsius; the fan remained off. No repair or parts use was recorded.

Gateway GW-19 uses a Raspberry Pi 5 with its fan-control defaults unchanged. During warm-up from a cold start, the reported temperature rose from 35 to 45 degrees Celsius; the fan remained off. No repair or parts use was recorded.

{"id": "REF-RP-PI5-FAN", "type": "reference"}
Raspberry Pi 5 defaults keep the fan off below 50 degrees Celsius during warming. Speeds at 50, 60, 67.5, and 75 degrees Celsius are respectively 30%, 50%, 70%, and 100%. Configuration can change these defaults.

{"id": "REF-RP-PI5-HYST", "type": "reference"}
As Raspberry Pi 5 cools, fan-speed reductions occur 5 degrees Celsius below the warming thresholds. This hysteresis and the speed thresholds are configurable.

input_sources.text: Gateway GW-18 uses a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B with default thermal settings. During this observation the SoC temperature rose to 82 degrees Celsius and the Arm clock decreased. The GPU clock was not measured. No maintenance or parts use was recorded.
Between 80 and 85 degrees Celsius, Raspberry Pi Arm cores progressively throttle. At 85 degrees Celsius, both Arm and GPU throttle. This describes thermal behavior, not a completed repair.
input_sources.attribution: Raspberry Pi Ltd; passages summarized by the project assistant.

input_sources.text: The documented vcgencmd measure_temp command reads the current SoC temperature through the GPU. Linux temperature readings can differ because of the monitoring implementation.
input_sources.attribution: Raspberry Pi Ltd; passages summarized by the project assistant.

original_sources.text: Gateway GW-18 uses a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B with default thermal settings. During this observation the SoC temperature rose to 82 degrees Celsius and the Arm clock decreased. The GPU clock was not measured. No maintenance or parts use was recorded.

source_items.transcription:
{"id": "RG-002-N1", "type": "field_note"}
Gateway GW-18 uses a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B with default thermal settings. During this observation the SoC temperature rose to 82 degrees Celsius and the Arm clock decreased. The GPU clock was not measured. No maintenance or parts use was recorded.

{"id": "REF-RP-THERMAL", "type": "reference"}
Between 80 and 85 degrees Celsius, Raspberry Pi Arm cores progressively throttle. At 85 degrees Celsius, both Arm and GPU throttle. This describes thermal behavior, not a completed repair.

{"id": "REF-RP-TEMPERATURE", "type": "reference"}
The documented vcgencmd measure_temp command reads the current SoC temperature through the GPU. Linux temperature readings can differ because of the monitoring implementation.
